Definition: to flaunt, i.e. raise a flag; figuratively, to be conspicuous
KeyPassages: Psalms 20:5; Song of Solomon 5:10; Song of Solomon 6:4; Song of Solomon 6:10
BiblicalUsage: To raise a banner is to make yourself seen, and the word carries both the battle standard and the lover's boast. The psalmist vows to set up banners in the name of God when salvation comes, and the Song pictures the beloved as terrible as an army with banners, beautiful and impossible to ignore. The same word names the one who stands out among ten thousand.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God gives His people a banner worth raising, and it is His name, not our own. When we lift Him up, we are seen for what we are: His, and marching under His standard.
